beginner.headline: Matthew Rhys Wins Two Emmys, Makes History
beginner.brief: Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys made history at the Emmys. He won two lead acting prizes in one night. He won for best lead actor in a limited series and for a comedy. At the start of his career, Rhys considered joining the British Army. He later received a rejection letter and could not join the army. Rhys speaks Welsh to his son Sam at home in New York. He also voices Han Solo in a new Welsh language adaptation of Star Wars.

intermediate.headline: Matthew Rhys: Welsh Performer Makes Emmy History and Shares Cultural Pride
intermediate.brief: Matthew Rhys, a Welsh performer, recently made Emmy history by winning two lead acting awards in one night. He received one award for a psychological thriller and another for a comedy series. Earlier in his career, Rhys was so desperate for employment that he thought about joining the British Army. However, an army officer was suspicious of him because he was a performer, and Rhys was later rejected. Years later, Rhys moved to Hollywood and lived with other Welsh performers, including Michael Sheen and Ioan Gruffudd. They would speak Welsh to each other and watch rugby games together in a British pub. Rhys is married to actress Keri Russell, and they have a son named Sam, whom Rhys hopes will understand the Welsh language. He also owns a 1939 wooden boat named Rarebit, which is also a traditional Welsh dish. Rhys's first language is Welsh, and he regularly uses it at home in New York. The passionate Welshman dedicated his second Emmy award to the great and good people of Wales. He said, "We are a small but mighty nation," expressing pride in his heritage. Rhys has also been revealed as the voice of Han Solo in a new Welsh language adaptation of Star Wars. This project, which required translating well-known phrases, brought up some unexpected feelings for Rhys.

advanced.headline: Matthew Rhys: Emmy History-Maker and Welsh Cultural Ambassador
advanced.brief: Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys has made history at the Emmys by becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night. He was named best lead actor in a limited series for the psychological thriller The Beast In Me , and best lead actor in a comedy for his role in Widow's Bay. Early in his career, Rhys seriously considered enlisting in the British Army due to a significant lack of acting opportunities. For nearly two years afterwards, he couldn't secure work, which deepened his resolve to explore alternatives. He later received a formal communication from the army, politely declining his application, which he found ironically telling. In 2006, Rhys moved to Hollywood and surrounded himself with fellow Welsh actors, including Michael Sheen and Ioan Gruffudd. He affectionately called their expatriate group the "LA Tafia," reflecting their shared Welsh roots in Los Angeles. Rhys met Keri Russell in Los Angeles at a kickball game in 2002, initially leaving a drunken message she found far from charming. A decade later, the pair finally became an item when they starred together as Russian spies in the TV series The Americans. Rhys owns a 1939 wooden cruiser boat, named Rarebit, which shares its name with a traditional Welsh dish of seasoned melted cheese on toast. He admitted not foreseeing "the disaster of buying an old wooden boat" before making the purchase, highlighting the challenges of its upkeep. The Welshman dedicated his second award to "the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurture as anyone else," expressing profound gratitude. Rhys is also recognized as the voice of Han Solo in an upcoming Welsh language rendition of Star Wars. This project, which involves translating familiar Star Wars elements into Welsh, elicited unexpected feelings for him. He remains keen to stay connected to all things Welsh, notably taking on the role of iconic Richard Burton in a one-man show in 2025.
